items.title: Try a 10 to 20 minute walk after dinner
items.text: Taking a walk after a meal is linked to a smaller rise in sugar, with the biggest difference seen after dinner. Walking for 10 to 19 minutes seems to be enough to get most of the benefit, with a rise about 17.5 mg/dL smaller.

items.title: Keep dinner early
items.text: Try not to eat dinner too late, as sugar tends to rise more after late dinners, about 9.2 mg/dL more. Only about 7.7% of your dinners are at 8 pm or later, so you're already doing a good job.

items.title: Aim for a 13-hour overnight break
items.text: You're averaging 12.1 hours of overnight fasting, which is a good habit to keep up. About 33.3% of nights you're reaching 13 hours of fasting, which might be helpful in combination with other coaching.
